actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Depth-relevant Features in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive feature analysis on a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model to identify potential depth-relevant features that can be leveraged for monocular depth estimation. Specifically, extract features from the model's intermediate layers and use correlation analysis with ground-truth depth maps to identify which features are most predictive of depth.
CONTROLS: Compare feature importance with and without visual pretext tasks that explicitly encourage depth estimation (e.g., predicting objects distances).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Top-ranked features will show strong correlations with depth, indicating the existence of depth-relevant information in pre-trained T2I models. However, the feature importance may not fully generalize across different datasets and scenes.

Expect the feature analysis to reveal a subset of features that are highly correlated with depth, suggesting that pre-trained T2I models indeed contain some depth-related knowledge. This study will lay the groundwork for subsequent research exploring how to extract and adapt these features for vision-and-language tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Soft-Weighting Techniques for Selective Fine-Tuning of Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Introduce soft-weighting techniques to selectively fine-tune specific layers or parts of the pre-trained text-to-image model for depth estimation, allowing for adaptation to depth data without degrading the original image generation capability. Specifically, use mixture weights to softly combine the pre-trained model weights with fine-tuned weights for depth estimation.
CONTROLS: Compare soft-weighting techniques with and without partial fine-tuning (i.e., only fine-tuning specific layers), as well as with full parameter fine-tuning for baseline comparisons.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Soft-weighting techniques will yield competitive depth estimation results with significantly less degradation of image generation quality compared to full-parameter fine-tuning. However, the choice of mixture weights and fine-tuning schedule may require careful hyperparameter tuning.

These techniques have the potential to mitigate the trade-off between depth estimation and image generation in pre-trained T2I models, enabling more flexible adaptation to diverse downstream tasks with minimal loss of original capabilities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Depth-guided Diffusion Process for Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Modify the pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model to incorporate an adaptive depth-guided process that utilizes the soft-weighted features extracted from the previous proposal to guide the denoising steps. This adaptation will aim to capture scene-specific depth relationships while minimizing degradation of the image generation quality.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed adaptation method against both full-parameter fine-tuning and partial fine-tuning, as well as baseline models without any adaptation.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The adaptive depth-guided diffusion process will significantly improve depth estimation accuracy while preserving the image generation quality of the pre-trained model. However, the adaptive mechanism might be sensitive to the choice of mixture weights, initial depth estimates, and scene complexity.

This approach addresses the challenge of extracting localized depth information from pre-trained T2I models while maintaining their original capabilities. The adaptability of the diffusion process will be crucial for handling diverse depth relationships in various scenes.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Adjusting REVISED 3: Adaptive Depth-guided Diffusion Process for Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Revise the adaptive depth-guided diffusion process to incorporate an auxiliary depth-specific loss term, which aims to enforce consistent depth estimates across the diffusion process. This modification will strengthen the model's ability to capture coherent scene depth structures, leading to more accurate estimates.
CONTROLS: Compare the revised process with and without the auxiliary loss term, as well as with other depth-related adaptations (e.g., depth-based feature normalizations).
COST: 400 GPU-hours (revised)
PREDICTION: The inclusion of the auxiliary loss term will significantly enhance the model's capacity for depth estimation, outperforming the original adaptive process in complex scenes. However, the auxiliary term might introduce additional instability during training, requiring further fine-tuning of the learning rate schedule.

By adding the depth-specific loss term, the revised process will better handle fine-grained depth relationships and improve overall depth estimation accuracy. This adjustment is crucial for adapting pre-trained T2I models to various monocular depth estimation tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Robust Bootstrap for Depth Enhancement in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Propose a robust bootstrap process that utilizes a dataset of random image-depth pairs to enhance the pre-trained text-to-image model's depth estimation capability. This process involves adjusting the model's feature space and diffusion process to better capture depth patterns and relationships.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the bootstrap process in conjunction with other adaptations (e.g., adaptive diffusion process, auxiliary loss term).
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The robust bootstrap process will further enhance the model's depth estimation capacity, allowing for more accurate and robust predictions across various scenes and datasets. However, the choice of initial random image-depth pairs might be critical for the bootstrap process to succeed.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Enhancing Depth Estimation in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models via Self-Supervised Learning
PROPOSAL: Revise the adaptive depth-guided diffusion process to a self-supervised learning framework, where the pre-trained text-to-image model is trained to predict depths from images it has never seen before. This new framework aims to learn generalizable depth patterns and relationships from large-scale, unlabelled data.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed framework against both full-parameter fine-tuning and other adaptations (e.g., adaptive diffusion process, auxiliary loss term).
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The self-supervised learning framework will promote more robust and generalizable depth estimation capabilities, allowing the model to perform well on unseen scenes and datasets. However, the choice of pre-training data and learning objectives might be crucial for the framework to succeed.

By employing self-supervised learning, the revised framework will effectively learn to generalize depth patterns across various scenes and data modalities, enabling more accurate and versatile depth estimation. This adjustment is crucial for adapting pre-trained T2I models to real-world depth estimation tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploiting Surface Normal Estimation Capabilities in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate whether pre-trained text-to-image models can leverage their existing capabilities for surface normal estimation to improve depth estimation accuracy. Specifically, develop a novel loss function that synthesizes surface normal estimates with depth estimates to enhance the model's ability to capture detailed scene geometry.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed loss function against other surface normal based adaptations.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The incorporation of surface normal estimates will enable the model to capture finer-grained scene geometry and depth patterns, leading to improved depth estimation accuracy. However, the novel loss function might require careful optimization to avoid over-fitting to specific scene structures.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Identifying Subnetworks for Depth Estimation in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Revise the feature analysis approach by identifying specific subnetworks within the pre-trained text-to-image model that are most relevant for depth estimation. This will involve pruning or masking individual components to understand the impact on depth estimation accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the subnetworks identified with the full model and other adaptations (e.g., self-supervised learning framework).
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The subnetworks identified will show a significant impact on depth estimation accuracy, with some subnetworks being more relevant than others for specific scenes and datasets. However, the pruning or masking process might require careful hyperparameter tuning to avoid over- or under-estimation of depth.

This revised approach will provide a more detailed understanding of which components within the pre-trained text-to-image model are crucial for depth estimation, allowing for targeted improvements and adaptations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Zero-Shot Monocular Depth Estimation via Text-to-Image Model-based Inversion
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel zero-shot depth estimation approach that leverages the text-to-image model's inversion capabilities to directly infer depth maps from image inputs. This will involve training a separate inversion model on a dataset of image-depth pairs to learn a mapping between the image space and depth space.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed approach against other zero-shot depth estimation methods (e.g., using visual pretext tasks).
COST: 700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The text-to-image model-based inversion approach will yield competitive depth estimation results without requiring any fine-tuning of the pre-trained model. However, the inversion model might require additional training data and careful hyperparameter tuning to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Robustness and Transferability of Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models for Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness and transferability of the depth estimation capabilities of pre-trained text-to-image models across various datasets, scenes, and datasets with different resolutions and lighting conditions. This will involve evaluating the models on a battery of depth estimation benchmarks and analyzing the impact of adversarial attacks on depth estimates.
CONTROLS: Compare the robustness and transferability of the pre-trained models with other adaptations (e.g., self-supervised learning framework, subnetwork pruning).
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The analysis will reveal that the pre-trained text-to-image models exhibit varying degrees of robustness and transferability, with some models being more resilient to adversarial attacks and dataset shifts. However, the models might struggle to generalize to extreme lighting conditions or novel scenes.

This study will provide insights into the limitations of pre-trained text-to-image models for depth estimation and inform the design of more robust and transferable adaptations.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Selective Fine-Tuning with Layer-wise Attention for Depth Estimation in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Revise the soft-weighting technique to incorporate layer-wise attention mechanisms, allowing the model to selectively focus on specific layers or modules during fine-tuning for depth estimation. This will involve introducing learnable weights to control the contribution of each layer to the depth estimation task.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the revised technique against other adaptations (e.g., self-supervised learning framework, subnetwork pruning).
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The layer-wise attention mechanism will enable the model to selectively adapt to the depth estimation task, leading to improved accuracy and robustness. However, the learnable weights might require careful optimization to avoid over-fitting to specific layers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multimodal Fusion for Depth Estimation in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the possibility of fusing depth estimates from multiple sources (e.g., pre-trained text-to-image model, other depth estimation models) to improve accuracy. This will involve developing a novel multimodal fusion framework that leverages the strengths of each source to produce more accurate depth estimates.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed framework against other multimodal fusion approaches and adaptations (e.g., self-supervised learning framework, subnetwork pruning).
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The multimodal fusion framework will lead to improved depth estimation accuracy by combining the strengths of multiple sources. However, the fusion process might require careful tuning to avoid over- or under-estimation of depth and to ensure that the fused model is robust and generalizable.

This study will demonstrate the effectiveness of multimodal fusion for depth estimation and provide a foundation for exploring more advanced fusion techniques and architectures.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Subnetwork Pruning for Depth Estimation in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models: A Global vs. Local Approach
PROPOSAL: Revise the subnetwork pruning approach to consider both global and local pruning strategies. The global approach will prune entire subnetworks, while the local approach will selectively prune specific neurons or layers within subnetworks. This will involve evaluating the impact of each pruning strategy on depth estimation accuracy and robustness.
CONTROLS: Compare the pruning strategies with other adaptations (e.g., self-supervised learning framework, multimodal fusion).
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The local pruning strategy will be more effective for depth estimation, as it allows for more targeted pruning of specific layers or neurons. However, the pruning process might require careful tuning to avoid under-estimation of depth and to ensure robustness.

TITLE: Depth Estimation in Pre-trained Text-to-Image Models: A Comprehensive Survey and Analysis
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive review of the existing literature on depth estimation in pre-trained text-to-image models, including the various approaches, techniques, and architectures discussed in this proposal. This will involve analyzing the strengths and weaknesses of each approach, identifying trends and insights, and recommending future research directions.
CONTROLS: None
COST: N/A (theoretical work)
PREDICTION: This survey will provide a comprehensive and structured overview of the current state of research on depth estimation in pre-trained text-to-image models, highlighting key insights, challenges, and opportunities for future research.

This final proposal will serve as a synthesis of the research project, providing a deep understanding of the complexities and challenges of depth estimation in pre-trained text-to-image models. The survey will be a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to understand the current landscape and inform their future work on this topic.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Depth Estimation through Prior-Preserved Denoising
PROPOSAL: We will introduce a novel depth estimation method that fine-tunes the denoising process of a pre-trained T2I diffusion model, while constraining the model's parameters to preserve its original image generation capabilities. This is achieved through an additional, carefully designed penalty term added to the loss function, which encourages the preservation of the model's original imaging-related weights.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance against a baseline that conducts standard full-parameter fine-tuning on a state-of-the-art T2I diffusion model.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect this method to produce competitive depth estimation results compared to full-parameter fine-tuning, while maintaining the pre-trained model's image generation quality. However, we may encounter difficulties in finding an optimal penalty term that effectively balances depth estimation quality and image generation preservation.

Turn 1 evaluates the effectiveness of preserving the original T2I model's image generation capabilities while introducing depth estimation ability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradual and Controlled Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose a gradual and controlled knowledge transfer mechanism to adapt the pre-trained T2I diffusion model for depth estimation without degrading its original image generation capability. This approach consists of iteratively adding a small amount of learnable depth-related parameters to the model, with each iteration retraining the updated parameters through a mixed objective function combining depth estimation and image generation loss metrics. We will employ a stepwise profile to control the convergence of the additional weights.
CONTROLS:  We will compare the performance of the proposed approach against the baseline of full-parameter fine-tuning and against proposal 1's prior-preserved denoising method, specifically evaluating the effect of parameter addition and convergence profile on depth estimation accuracy and image generation quality.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed approach to yield competitive depth estimation performance while preserving the original image generation quality, due to its ability to iteratively adapt the model to depth estimation without needing to extensively retrain its weight parameters.

Turn 2 aims to find a middle ground between fixed and full-parameter adaptation, leveraging controlled knowledge transfer for a capacity distribution.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Gradual and Controlled Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose to revise proposal 2 by incorporating an attentive mechanism to selectively focus on depth-related features during the iterative adaptation process. This will allow the model to selectively absorb depth-related knowledge without overwriting the original image generation capacity. Specifically, we will use a depth-aware attention module to dynamically weight the importance of different feature maps in the denoising step, enabling the model to better differentiate between depth-related and image-related features.
CONTROLS:  The revised approach will be compared against the original proposal 2, as well as the full-parameter fine-tuning baseline and prior-preserved denoising method.
COST: 120 GPU-hours (revision of existing experiment)
PREDICTION: We expect the revised approach to improve depth estimation performance while maintaining the original image generation quality, by more effectively leveraging the depth-related information contained in the pre-trained T2I model.

By introducing the attentive mechanism, Turn 3 aims to enhance the model's ability to selectively incorporate depth-related knowledge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Multi-Task Loss Framework
PROPOSAL: We will design a hierarchical multi-task loss framework that offsets the competition between image generation and depth estimation by structuring the objective function into multiple, hierarchical layers. In the lower layers, we will retain the original image generation loss function, with additional depth estimation loss terms added in higher layers to guide the model's learning process. This approach aims to allow the model to refine its depth estimation capabilities while preventing the degradation of its image generation quality.
CONTROLS: The proposed hierarchical framework will be compared against the full-parameter fine-tuning baseline and prior-preserved denoising method, with particular focus on the interplay between depth estimation accuracy and image generation quality.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed hierarchical loss framework to yield competitive depth estimation performance and preserve the original image generation quality, due to its ability to decouple the competition between image generation and depth estimation tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Depth-Aware Implicit Denoising
PROPOSAL: We propose an implicit denoising mechanism that learns depth-related denoising distributions during the inference process. This distribution-based approach allows the model to adaptively generate depth-related noise schedules that are tailored to the specific scene depths being estimated. By leveraging depth-related side information from both the input image and the pre-trained T2I model, the proposed method has the potential to improve depth estimation accuracy while maintaining original image generation quality.
CONTROLS: The proposed implicit denoising method will be evaluated on a selection of test images, and performance will be compared against the full-parameter fine-tuning baseline and prior-preserved denoising method.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (.requires inference-only compute)
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed implicit denoising approach to yield state-of-the-art depth estimation results, by effectively estimating and leveraging depth-related noise distributions. Challenges may arise in optimizing the model to generate these distributions efficiently.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Depth Estimation in Pre-Trained T2I Models
PROPOSAL: This theoretical result will investigate the information-theoretic aspects of depth estimation in pre-trained T2I models, focusing on the relationship between the model's capacity to represent depth information and its original image generation capability. We will derive bounds on the mutual information between depth channels and the image generation process, and analyze the implications of these bounds for efficient depth estimation in T2I models.
CONTROLS: N/A (Theory-only proposal)
COST: 0 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The analysis is expected to reveal theoretical insights into the existing trade-offs between image generation and depth estimation in pre-trained T2I models, and provide design principles for optimizing the depth estimation process in such models.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Gradient Regularization for Prior-Preserved Denoising
PROPOSAL: We propose to revise the prior-preserved denoising approach (proposal 1) by incorporating gradient regularization to further improve the preservation of the pre-trained T2I model's original image generation capability. By minimizing the divergence of the gradients of the model's original image generation objective function and its adapated objective function for depth estimation, the revised method aims to ensure that the additional depth estimation parameters do not disturb the original model's learning dynamics.
CONTROLS: The revised approach will be compared against the original prior-preserved denoising method, the full-parameter fine-tuning baseline, and the hierarchical multi-task loss framework.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (revision of existing experiment)
PREDICTION: We expect the revised method to yield improved depth estimation accuracy and preserve the original image generation quality, by providing additional regularization to the prior-preserved denoising approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Estimation for Monocular Images
PROPOSAL: We propose an uncertainty-aware depth estimation approach that utilizes the Monte Carlo dropout method to approximate the model's depth estimation uncertainty. This will enable the model to produce depth estimates with accompanying confidence measures, allowing for better evaluation and selection of reliable estimates. We will apply this approach to the output of our pre-trained T2I model, and evaluate its effectiveness in scenarios where uncertainty estimation is valuable.
CONTROLS: The proposed uncertainty-aware depth estimation approach will be compared against traditional methods for uncertainty estimation in depth estimation, such as ensembling and output entropy-based methods.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed approach to yield competitive depth estimation results with uncertainty estimates that are highly informative, particularly in challenging scenarios with varying levels of outlier variances. Challenges may arise in modeling the uncertainty at high resolutions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Surface Normal Estimation as a By-Product of Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We will propose a surface normal estimation approach that leverages the depth estimation capabilities of the pre-trained T2I model, by utilizing the geometry-preserved priors learned from the model's original image generation task. We will show that with minimal modifications to the loss function and inference process, our pre-trained model can produce competitive surface normal estimates, suggesting an economical and efficient approach to integrating monocular depth and surface normal estimation tasks.
CONTROLS: The proposed surface normal estimation method will be compared against traditional hand-crafted surface normal estimation techniques and other methods that were specifically fine-tuned for surface normal estimation.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed method to yield competitive surface normal estimation results, with a significant reduction in computational overhead and without extensive model fine-tuning, taking advantage of the pre-trained visual prior for efficient geometry preservation estimation. Challenges may arise in cases of ambiguous surface normal configuations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensembling for Robust Monocular Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We will propose an ensemble approach that aggregates predictions from different proposals (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7) to obtain more robust and accurate depth estimation results. We will investigate how to selectively combine the strengths of each individual method, leveraging their unique strengths in different scenarios, such as high-quality images vs. low-quality images, or depth maps with high vs. low gradient scales.
CONTROLS: The ensemble approach will be compared against individual proposals, as well as traditional ensemble methods that combine different models estimated separately. 
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed ensemble method to significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of monocular depth estimation, by effectively combining the strengths of the individual proposals and mitigating their weaknesses. Challenges may arise in exploring an optimal ensemble method that balances model complexity with generalization performance.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Hybrid Conditioning for Efficient Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose using a meta-loss that incorporates the learned depth map as an additional conditioning input to the pre-trained diffusion model's UNET/denoising networks. This conditioning process is inspired by self-attention mechanisms, which naturally propagate spatial contextual information. Specifically, we append an adaptive fusion block that self-attends with both the original observation and the learned depth map. This will allow the model to selectively focus on parts of the image that are most relevant to depth estimation while maintaining the original image generation capability.
CONTROLS: Baseline proposal directly fine-tunes the pre-trained model without any additional conditioning; ablation study where the adaptive fusion block is replaced with a simple concatenation or feature patching.
COST: Estimated 10 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect a significant improvement in depth estimation accuracy with minimal degradation in image quality. It could fail if the adaptive fusion block is not optimized properly or if the conditioning input does not contribute sufficiently to the depth estimation process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Depth-Aware CLIP: Depth Prediction through Auxiliary Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose extending the vision-and-language CLIP framework by adding an auxiliary depth prediction task. CLIP learns a common embedding space for images and text, which we leverage for depth estimation by pre-training a CLIP model with an auxiliary task that predicts depth maps from the learned image representations. During pre-training, the CLIP model is fine-tuned on a depth estimation dataset, leading to the development of a depth-aware image representation that captures depth information while keeping the original image generation capability intact.
CONTROLS: Control experiments include baseline CLIP model without the auxiliary depth prediction task, and an ablation study where the CLIP model is trained on different datasets for depth estimation.
COST: Estimated 20 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect the CLIP-based depth estimation framework to reach competitive depth estimation performance compared to state-of-the-art models while maintaining the original image generation capability. It might fail if the pre-trained CLIP model's image representations are not sufficiently informative for depth estimation or if the auxiliary task overfits to the pre-training depth dataset.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Depth-Aware CLIP: Depth Prediction through Auxiliary Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We revise the previous proposal by incorporating a depth-aware loss during the pre-training phase of CLIP. Specifically, we add a multi-task loss that combines the standard CLIP loss with a depth-aware loss, which encourages the model to predict depth maps from the learned image representations. This approach allows the model to learn a more informed and depth-aware image representation that captures both visual and depth information.
CONTROLS: Controls include the original CLIP model without the auxiliary depth prediction task, and an ablation study where the depth-aware loss is replaced with a standard depth loss or removed altogether.
COST: Estimated 25 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect the revised CLIP model to achieve improved depth estimation performance compared to the original CLIP model and the previous baseline (Turn 1). The depth-aware loss could potentially negatively impact the original image generation capability if not optimized properly.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Depth-Aware CLIP: Depth Prediction through Auxiliary Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We revise the previous proposal by incorporating a depth-aware loss during the pre-training phase of CLIP. Specifically, we add a multi-task loss that combines the standard CLIP loss with a depth-aware loss, which encourages the model to predict depth maps from the learned image representations. This approach allows the model to learn a more informed and depth-aware image representation that captures both visual and depth information.
CONTROLS: Controls include the original CLIP model without the auxiliary depth prediction task, and an ablation study where the depth-aware loss is replaced with a standard depth loss or removed altogether.
COST: Estimated 25 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect the revised CLIP model to achieve improved depth estimation performance compared to the original CLIP model and the previous baseline (Turn 1). The depth-aware loss could potentially negatively impact the original image generation capability if not optimized properly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Fusion of Depth and Image Features
PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical fusion module that combines the feature representations from the depth estimation and image generation tasks in a multi-resolution manner. The module consists of multiple fusion blocks, each of which combines features from both tasks at a specific resolution. The combined features are then fed into a downstream depth estimation module to produce the final depth map. This approach allows the model to effectively share knowledge between tasks and leverage the strengths of both depth estimation and image generation.
CONTROLS: Controls include the baseline model that does not use hierarchical fusion, and an ablation study where the number of fusion blocks is varied or the fusion mechanism is changed (e.g., from concatenation to addition).
COST: Estimated 30 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect the hierarchical fusion module to achieve improved depth estimation performance by effectively combining task-specific features. The effectiveness of the module might be limited if the feature representations from the depth estimation and image generation tasks are not sufficiently complementary or if the number of fusion blocks is not optimized.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Knowledge Distillation for Zero-Shot Depth Estimation from Pre-Training
PROPOSAL: We propose using knowledge distillation to transfer the depth estimation knowledge from a pre-trained diffusion model to a smaller teacher-student architecture. The teacher model is the pre-trained diffusion model, while the student model is a smaller version of the same model architecture. The teacher model is used to generate synthetic depth maps during training, which are then used to train the student model. This approach allows the student model to learn the depth estimation task without requiring extensive re-training on depth-specific data.
CONTROLS: Controls include the baseline model that is trained from scratch on depth data, and an ablation study where the student model is initialized with random weights or the distillation process is modified (e.g., using different loss functions).
COST: Estimated 15 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect the knowledge distillation approach to achieve competitive depth estimation performance with minimal training overhead. The approach might fail if the teacher-student architecture is not well-matched or if the distillation process is not effective in transferring the knowledge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Asymmetric Attention for Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose using an asymmetric attention mechanism to selectively focus on depth-relevant regions in the input image. The mechanism consists of a spatial attention branch that learns to focus on regions of interest and a channel attention branch that learns to selectively weigh the importance of different feature channels. The output of the two branches is then combined to produce a final depth estimation.
CONTROLS: Controls include the baseline model that does not use attention, and an ablation study where the spatial or channel attention branch is removed or modified.
COST: Estimated 12 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect the asymmetric attention mechanism to improve depth estimation performance by effectively focusing on relevant regions in the input image. The mechanism might not be effective if the attention process is not properly regularized or if the learned attention weights do not accurately represent the depth-relevant regions.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Asymmetric Attention for Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We revise the previous proposal by incorporating a learnable spatial attention mask that adapts to the input image. The spatial attention branch learns to predict a binary mask that indicates the relevant regions in the image, and this mask is then used to selectively attend to these regions. Additionally, we introduce a correlation layer to analyze the spatial correlation between the attended regions and the input image, which further improves the depth estimation performance.
CONTROLS: Controls include the original asymmetric attention mechanism, and an ablation study where the learnable spatial attention mask or the correlation layer is removed or modified.
COST: Estimated 18 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect the revised asymmetric attention mechanism to achieve improved depth estimation performance by more effectively attending to relevant regions in the input image. The mechanism might not work well if the spatial attention mask or the correlation layer is not properly regularized or if the learned attention weights do not accurately represent the depth-relevant regions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Image Generation and Depth Estimation via Progressive Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a progressive transfer learning framework that starts with pre-training the diffusion model on image generation tasks and then gradually transfers the knowledge to depth estimation tasks. The framework might not be effective if the pre-trained model does not capture sufficient shared representations or if the progressive transfer learning scheme is not properly regularized.

PROPOSAL 1: Adaptive Hybrid Conditioning for Efficient Depth Estimation
We propose using a meta-loss that incorporates the learned depth map as an additional conditioning input to the pre-trained diffusion model's UNET/denoising networks. This conditioning process is inspired by self-attention mechanisms, which naturally propagate spatial contextual information. Specifically, we append an adaptive fusion block that self-attends with both the original observation and the learned depth map. This will allow the model to selectively focus on parts of the image that are most relevant to depth estimation while maintaining the original image generation capability.
Controls: Baseline proposal directly fine-tunes the pre-trained model without any additional conditioning; ablation study where the adaptive fusion block is replaced with a simple concatenation or feature patching.
Estimated cost: Estimated 10 GPU-hours.
Prediction: We expect a significant improvement in depth estimation accuracy with minimal degradation in image quality. It could fail if the adaptive fusion block is not optimized properly or if the conditioning input does not contribute sufficiently to the depth estimation process.

PROPOSAL 2: Depth-Aware CLIP: Depth Prediction through Auxiliary Contrastive Learning
We revise the previous proposal by incorporating a depth-aware loss during the pre-training phase of CLIP. Specifically, we add a multi-task loss that combines the standard CLIP loss with a depth-aware loss, which encourages the model to predict depth maps from the learned image representations. This approach allows the model to learn a more informed and depth-aware image representation that captures both visual and depth information.
Controls: Controls include the original CLIP model without the auxiliary depth prediction task, and an ablation study where the depth-aware loss is replaced with a standard depth loss or removed altogether.
Estimated cost: Estimated 25 GPU-hours.
Prediction: We expect the revised CLIP model to achieve improved depth estimation performance compared to the original CLIP model and the previous baseline (Turn 1). The depth-aware loss could potentially negatively impact the original image generation capability if not optimized properly.

PROPOSAL 3: Hierarchical Fusion of Depth and Image Features
We propose a hierarchical fusion module that combines the feature representations from the depth estimation and image generation tasks in a multi-resolution manner. The module consists of multiple fusion blocks, each of which combines features from both tasks at a specific resolution. The combined features are then fed into a downstream depth estimation module to produce the final depth map. This approach allows the model to effectively share knowledge between tasks and leverage the strengths of both depth estimation and image generation.
Controls: Controls include the baseline model that does not use hierarchical fusion, and an ablation study where the number of fusion blocks is varied or the fusion mechanism is changed (e.g., from concatenation to addition).
Estimated cost: Estimated 30 GPU-hours.
Prediction: We expect the hierarchical fusion module to achieve improved depth estimation performance by effectively combining task-specific features. The effectiveness of the module might be limited if the feature representations from the depth estimation and image generation tasks are not sufficiently complementary or if the number of fusion blocks is not optimized.

PROPOSAL 4: Knowledge Distillation for Zero-Shot Depth Estimation from Pre-Training
We propose using knowledge distillation to transfer the depth estimation knowledge from a pre-trained diffusion model to a smaller teacher-student architecture. The teacher model is the pre-trained diffusion model, while the student model is a smaller version of the same model architecture. The teacher model is used to generate synthetic depth maps during training, which are then used to train the student model. This approach allows the student model to learn the depth estimation task without requiring extensive re-training on depth-specific data.
Controls: Controls include the baseline model that is trained from scratch on depth data, and an ablation study where the student model is initialized with random weights or the distillation process is modified (e.g., using different loss functions).
Estimated cost: Estimated 15 GPU-hours.
Prediction: We expect the knowledge distillation approach to achieve competitive depth estimation performance with minimal training overhead. The approach might fail if the teacher-student architecture is not well-matched or if the distillation process is not effective in transferring the knowledge.

PROPOSAL 5: Asymmetric Attention for Depth Estimation
We revise the previous proposal by incorporating a learnable spatial attention mask that adapts to the input image. The spatial attention branch learns to predict a binary mask that indicates the relevant regions in the image, and this mask is then used to selectively attend to these regions. Additionally, we introduce a correlation layer to analyze the spatial correlation between the attended regions and the input image, which further improves the depth estimation performance.
Controls: Controls include the original asymmetric attention mechanism, and an ablation study where the learnable spatial attention mask or the correlation layer is removed or modified.
Estimated cost: Estimated 18 GPU-hours.
Prediction: We expect the revised asymmetric attention mechanism to achieve improved depth estimation performance by more effectively attending to relevant regions in the input image. The mechanism might not work well if the spatial attention mask or the correlation layer is not properly regularized or if the learned attention weights do not accurately represent the depth-relevant regions.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sampling-Based Semantics-Aware Uncertainty Estimation for Free-Form Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Design an experiment to adapt and combine state-of-the-art methods for estimating predictive uncertainty in masked diffusion models (MDMs) and autoregressive models (ARMs) with a novel sampling strategy that leverages iterative rewriting and reactivation techniques to encourage semantic diversity. Compare MDMs and ARMs with ARM-specific methods, such as temperature scaling, and ablate the influence of semantic rewriting.
CONTROLS: Compare to state-of-the-art uncertainty estimation methods, ablate iterative rewriting, and use different hierarchical clustering algorithms to group semantically equivalent responses.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The experiment will show that MDMs can achieve comparable or better performance than ARMs in estimating aleatoric uncertainty when combined with our novel sampling strategy, while struggling to provide faithful estimates of epistemic uncertainty. 

The main risk of failure is over-sampling in a small budget constraint, leading to no semantic diversity within samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Epistemic Uncertainty Estimation via Bayesian Model Averaging of Language Models
PROPOSAL: Formulate a Bayesian model averaging (BMA) approach to estimate epistemic uncertainty by combining the output distributions of multiple pre-trained language models (LMs) using a hierarchical mixture model. We will implement BMA on both masked diffusion models (MDMs) and autoregressive models (ARMs) to compare their performance in estimating epistemic uncertainty and investigate the effect of model heterogeneity on uncertainty estimation.
CONTROLS: Compare to a single model approach, use different model combinations, and apply BMA to both real and synthetic data.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: BMA will lead to significantly better epistemic uncertainty estimates for both MDMs and ARMs, particularly when combining models of varying architectures, and bring substantial improvements over a single model approach. 

The main challenge lies in the computational cost and validating the assumption of model homoscedasticity, which may lead to biased uncertainty estimates when not met.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Clustering with Epistemic Guided Metrics for Evaluating Semantically Equivalent Outputs
PROPOSAL: Develop a hierarchical clustering approach with epistemic guided metrics that incorporates epistemic uncertainty estimates into the clustering process to evaluate semantically equivalent outputs. This method aims to identify the actual diversity in the semantic space while eliminating variance caused by aleatoric uncertainty. Integrating our approach with existing methods will enable more accurate evaluation of uncertainty estimates and response equivalence.
CONTROLS: Compare to standard hierarchical clustering algorithms (e.g., Ward, UPGMA, average-link), and use the BMA-based epistemic uncertainty estimates as input.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed approach leads to a more accurate evaluation of semantically equivalent outputs, allowing for a more precise estimation of aleatoric uncertainty and improving overall performance of uncertainty estimation methods.

The challenge is balancing the epistemic uncertainty weights to avoid introducing structure-bias in the resulting clusters, and experimenting with various thresholding techniques.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Hierarchical Clustering with Epistemic Guided Metrics for Evaluating Semantically Equivalent Outputs
PROPOSAL: Refine the hierarchical clustering approach to allow for the integration of Bayesian model-averaged epistemic uncertainty estimates, branching-off from hierarchical clustering of standard outputs. This revision enables us to compare the effects of purely semantic (including our rewritten samples) clustering with that incorporating actual model confidences, allowing for improved substance to the exploration of purely semantic clustering while offering a direction towards reliable estimation that learns naturally from data.

CONTROLS: Include baseline performances under varying sampling configurations, specifically for diverse and inaccurate sampling strategies (temperature scheduling and behavior cloning), using distance metrics acting upon word vectors indirectly typical of sentence sets.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The compared results on distance metrics methods provide vivid heightened impersonations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decomposing Epistemic Uncertainty into Data Coverage and Model Knowledge Gaps
PROPOSAL: Introduce a theoretical framework that decomposes epistemic uncertainty into two components: the data coverage gap and the model knowledge gap. The data coverage gap captures the model's inability to generalize to unseen data, while the model knowledge gap reflects the model's lack of knowledge or training data. We will analyze the relationships between these components and develop a novel algorithm to estimate them using BMA-based epistemic uncertainty estimates.
CONTROLS: Use the proposed decomposition to ablate the effect of each component on uncertainty estimation and evaluate the accuracy of the algorithm using real-world datasets.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The decomposition will provide valuable insights into the sources of epistemic uncertainty in LMs, and the algorithm will be able to accurately estimate the data coverage and model knowledge gaps, achieving up to 20% improvement in uncertainty estimation compared to current methods.

The main challenge lies in correctly formulating the relationships between the two components and developing a practical algorithm to estimate them, given the complexity of model uncertainty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight and Sample-Efficient Estimation of Semantic Aleatoric Uncertainty using Prompt-Based Representations
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel prompt-based approach to estimate semantic aleatoric uncertainty, leveraging the fact that different prompts can reveal distinct aspects of the model's output distribution. We will train prompt-based representations of the output distribution and use them to estimate uncertainty in a sample-efficient manner, reducing the number of generations required for accurate uncertainty estimation.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing methods that rely on hierarchical clustering and iterative rewriting, and evaluate the performance of different prompt-based representations.
COST: 60 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed approach will achieve comparable or better performance than existing methods, while requiring significantly fewer generations and being more scalable to large datasets. 

The main risk is selecting representations that are too coarse-grained or lack sufficient information for accurate uncertainty estimation, particularly when evaluating high-aleatoric-uncertainty scenarios (thereby also limiting improvements to correlative data points.)

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Lightweight and Sample-Efficient Estimation of Semantic Aleatoric Uncertainty using Prompt-Based Representations
PROPOSAL: Revise the prompt-based approach by incorporating information from multiple representative prompts to estimate semantic aleatoric uncertainty, increasing the reliability of the uncertainty estimates obtained. The proposed framework, PROMPT-U, aggregates and selects a set of informative prompts that are maximally informative about the output distribution. This results in more robust estimates of aleatoric uncertainty that capture nuanced variations in response semantics.

CONTROLS: Compare PROMPT-U with existing lightweight methods, and study how different prompt selection strategies impact PROMPT-U's performance.
COST: 90 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: PROMPT-U will significantly improve the accuracy of aleatoric uncertainty estimates and enhance robustness against variations in prompts and model architectures. 

However, the main risk of missing informative prompts might impact PROMPT-U's effectiveness for particular types of questions and require better signal-to-noise of other representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Encouragement of Semantic Diversity in Language Models
PROPOSAL: Introduce an adversarial training framework that fine-tunes language models to produce semantically diverse outputs, promoting more accurate uncertainty estimation. By introducing an adversary that selectively samples semantically equivalent outputs, we can stimulate the model to generate a broader range of possible responses, ultimately leading to improved uncertainty estimates.
CONTROLS: Compare to vanilla training, ablate the effect of different adversary architectures, and evaluate the impact on uncertainty estimation using real-world benchmarks.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed adversarial training framework will significantly improve the quality and diversity of outputs, leading to more accurate uncertainty estimates and potentially mitigating the effects of epistemic uncertainty in language models.

The main challenge lies in designing an effective adversary that selectively samples semantically equivalent outputs, as well as balancing the trade-off between promoting semantic diversity and maintaining model performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Model Selection for Improving Robustness to Adversarial Attacks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of uncertainty-focused model selection on improving the robustness of language models to adversarial attacks. We will leverage the uncertainty estimates from existing methods to select more robust models, specifically focusing on designing a sparse aggregator that learns to combine outputs from diverse models to combat the curse of over-reliance on deterministic models.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing robustness-enhancing methods and model selection strategies, ablate the effect of different aggregators, and evaluate the impact of uncertainty-aware model selection on robustness and performance.
COST: 160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed framework will lead to a significant improvement in the robustness of language models against adversarial attacks, reducing the fooling rate and mitigating the negative impact of epistemic uncertainty.

The main challenge lies in designing an effective aggregator that operates in high-dimensional spaces, selecting the optimal trade-off between robustness and performance, and evaluating the impact on practical scenarios.

ACTION: REVISE 7
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Model Selection for Improving Robustness to Adversarial Attacks
PROPOSAL: Revise the framework to learn a conditional distribution that models the uncertainty of a given model's output given its input and then employ this distribution for model selection. We incorporate robustness-aware Bayesian model-averaging techniques to enhance the uncertainty estimation module. The revised framework combines a geometry-aware uncertainty space exploration scheme with a hierarchical weighting strategy.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing robustness-enhancing methods, ablate the effect of different hierarchies and weighting strategies, and conduct extensive empirical evaluations.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised framework should lead to significantly improved robustness against adversarial attacks, combined with better uncertainty estimation for uncertainty-aware model selection and fewer implicit adoption biases when exploring the optimality under which the best class  is solely customizable under ready expectation.

We will implement BMA on both masked diffusion models (MDMs) and autoregressive models (ARMs) to compare their performance in estimating epistemic uncertainty and investigate the effect of model heterogeneity on uncertainty estimation.
Controls: Compare to a single model approach, use different model combinations, and apply BMA to both real and synthetic data.
Estimated cost: 150 GPU-hours
Prediction: BMA will lead to significantly better epistemic uncertainty estimates for both MDMs and ARMs, particularly when combining models of varying architectures, and bring substantial improvements over a single model approach. 

The main challenge lies in the computational cost and validating the assumption of model homoscedasticity, which may lead to biased uncertainty estimates when not met.

PROPOSAL 3: Hierarchical Clustering with Epistemic Guided Metrics for Evaluating Semantically Equivalent Outputs
Refine the hierarchical clustering approach to allow for the integration of Bayesian model-averaged epistemic uncertainty estimates, branching-off from hierarchical clustering of standard outputs. This revision enables us to compare the effects of purely semantic (including our rewritten samples) clustering with that incorporating actual model confidences, allowing for improved substance to the exploration of purely semantic clustering while offering a direction towards reliable estimation that learns naturally from data.

Estimated cost: 120 GPU-hours

PROPOSAL 4: Decomposing Epistemic Uncertainty into Data Coverage and Model Knowledge Gaps
Introduce a theoretical framework that decomposes epistemic uncertainty into two components: the data coverage gap and the model knowledge gap. The data coverage gap captures the model's inability to generalize to unseen data, while the model knowledge gap reflects the model's lack of knowledge or training data. We will analyze the relationships between these components and develop a novel algorithm to estimate them using BMA-based epistemic uncertainty estimates.
Controls: Use the proposed decomposition to ablate the effect of each component on uncertainty estimation and evaluate the accuracy of the algorithm using real-world datasets.
Estimated cost: 180 GPU-hours
Prediction: The decomposition will provide valuable insights into the sources of epistemic uncertainty in LMs, and the algorithm will be able to accurately estimate the data coverage and model knowledge gaps, achieving up to 20% improvement in uncertainty estimation compared to current methods.

The main challenge lies in correctly formulating the relationships between the two components and developing a practical algorithm to estimate them, given the complexity of model uncertainty.

PROPOSAL 5: Lightweight and Sample-Efficient Estimation of Semantic Aleatoric Uncertainty using Prompt-Based Representations
Revise the prompt-based approach by incorporating information from multiple representative prompts to estimate semantic aleatoric uncertainty, increasing the reliability of the uncertainty estimates obtained. The proposed framework, PROMPT-U, aggregates and selects a set of informative prompts that are maximally informative about the output distribution. This results in more robust estimates of aleatoric uncertainty that capture nuanced variations in response semantics.
Controls: Compare PROMPT-U with existing lightweight methods, and study how different prompt selection strategies impact PROMPT-U's performance.
Estimated cost: 90 GPU-hours
Prediction: PROMPT-U will significantly improve the accuracy of aleatoric uncertainty estimates and enhance robustness against variations in prompts and model architectures. 

However, the main risk of missing informative prompts might impact PROMPT-U's effectiveness for particular types of questions and require better signal-to-noise of other representations.

PROPOSAL 6: Adversarial Training for Robust Encouragement of Semantic Diversity in Language Models
Introduce an adversarial training framework that fine-tunes language models to produce semantically diverse outputs, promoting more accurate uncertainty estimation. By introducing an adversary that selectively samples semantically equivalent outputs, we can stimulate the model to generate a broader range of possible responses, ultimately leading to improved uncertainty estimates.
Controls: Compare to vanilla training, ablate the effect of different adversary architectures, and evaluate the impact on uncertainty estimation using real-world benchmarks.
Estimated cost: 120 GPU-hours
Prediction: The proposed adversarial training framework will significantly improve the quality and diversity of outputs, leading to more accurate uncertainty estimates and potentially mitigating the effects of epistemic uncertainty in language models.

The main challenge lies in designing an effective adversary that selectively samples semantically equivalent outputs, as well as balancing the trade-off between promoting semantic diversity and maintaining model performance.

PROPOSAL 7: Uncertainty-Aware Model Selection for Improving Robustness to Adversarial Attacks
Revise the framework to learn a conditional distribution that models the uncertainty of a given model's output given its input and then employ this distribution for model selection. We incorporate robustness-aware Bayesian model-averaging techniques to enhance the uncertainty estimation module. The revised framework combines a geometry-aware uncertainty space exploration scheme with a hierarchical weighting strategy.
Controls: Compare with existing robustness-enhancing methods, ablate the effect of different hierarchies and weighting strategies, and conduct extensive empirical evaluations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Inter-Slice Inconsistency in 2D Diffusion-Based 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the spatial variability of the 2D diffusion prior when applied slice-by-slice using a standard 2D diffusion model (e.g., DALL-E or StyleGAN2-ADA) with catastrophic correlation analysis on real-world datasets in medical imaging, such as the brain MRI isotropic super-resolution challenge (BRATS) and the sparse-view CT reconstruction archives (e.g., LoDoPaB-MLL-Hu, LoDoPaB-LL-Hu, or the SSC dataset).
CONTROLS: Baseline 2D reconstruction without any explicit regularization, evaluations of prior standard deviations across slices, and observations on reconstructed image features and correlations among spatially distant slices.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (network inference + pre-processing on a large real-world dataset for correlation analysis).
PREDICTION: Moderate to strong positive correlation (ρ > 0.5) between spatially adjacent slices for the aggregation of subtle image features such as fine texture and anatomical structures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation Study on Diffusion Sampling Steps
PROPOSAL: Revise the diffusion sampling process by synchronizing the stochastic noise components across slices in both the forward and reverse diffusion paths. Implement variants of the 2D diffusion-based 3D reconstruction pipeline that manipulate the sampling noise by applying the following remedies: intra-slice White Gaussian noise, inter-slice (“batch-wise”) synchronized White Gaussian noise, and reusing the same noise realization for all slices in a single forward single backward pass (aka, meta-stochastic synchronization). Evaluate these ablations on the same real-world medical imaging datasets.
CONTROLS: Baseline 2D reconstruction, along with the ablated variants where only the sampling noise component is changed, while the rest of the pipeline remains unaltered.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (variations of the existing network with slightly modified diffusion steps on a large real-world dataset for a thorough evaluation).
PREDICTION: Improvements over the standard 2D diffusion approach on metrics such as SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure) or PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) for spatial consistency, with significant conflict if the employed remedy unduly “softens” the image features.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantifying Slice-Wise Sampling Induced Inter-Slice Discontinuities
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the effect of inter-slice sampling on discontinuities using a standard 2D diffusion model trained on BrainWeb datasets and then applied to 3D reconstructions. We will measure the mean square error (MSE) between consecutive slices in the reconstructed volumes and compare it to the MSE of reconstructed volumes using a learned 3D diffusion model as an oracle to assess the performance cost of slice-wise sampling.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by the baseline of using a 2D diffusion model for 3D reconstruction with no noise injection in the sampling process.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the MSE between consecutive slices will increase with the number of slices (or the number of iterative reverse diffusion steps) and that slice-wise sampling will introduce more significant discontinuities than a learned 3D model. The proposed baseline of omitting noise injection might not completely eliminate discontinuities but should significantly reduce their severity, as it would likely induce low-amplitude random fluctuations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Effect of Stochasticity on Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: We will modify the proposed baseline of omitting noise injection in the sampling process by only removing the noise injection along the z-axis (vertical direction) while keeping it in the x and y directions (horizontal). This will help to understand the contribution of stochasticity along each dimension. We will then evaluate the effect on slice consistency metrics, such as the MSE between consecutive slices, and visually inspect the results using the BrainWeb dataset and our in-house 3DMRI dataset.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by the original baseline of omitting noise injection in the sampling process and explore how much each dimension contributes to the overall slice consistency.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that removing noise injection along the z-axis will result in the smallest improvement, and that horizontal noise injection will have a more significant impact on slice consistency. This could indicate that inter-slice discontinuities arise primarily from circulating noise during the diffusion sampling process.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhanced Inter-Slice Consistency Through Coordinate-Dependent Noise Injection
PROPOSAL: We will explore an alternative approach to reducing inter-slice discontinuities by controlling noise injection in a way that is coordinate-dependent. In particular, we will modify the sampling process to introduce noise along the z-axis (vertical direction) in a manner that is correlated across consecutive slices, rather than independent. This will be achieved by using a shared noise vector for consecutive slices, with a small amount of residual noise to mimic the natural fluctuations in the real data. We will train a 2D diffusion model on 3DMRI and BrainWeb datasets using this modified sampling process and evaluate its effect on slice consistency metrics, such as the MSE between consecutive slices, and visually inspect the results.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by the baseline approach of using a standard 2D diffusion model for 3D reconstruction and the modified baseline of omitting noise injection along the z-axis.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that this novel approach will significantly reduce inter-slice discontinuities, while maintaining or even improving the natural anatomical variation between slices, by effectively spreading out the correlated noise among consecutive slices. However, it may introduce computational and memory overheads due to the shared noise vector.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Analyzing the Effect of Stochasticity on Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: We will extend the previous proposal by incorporating an additional experiment where we freeze the noise injection schedule along the z-axis, thereby eliminating stochasticity along this dimension completely. We will then compare the results of this experiment to the previous two: omitting noise injection, and modifying the noise injection to be correlated. This will help us to better understand the relative impact of noise injection along the z-axis and how it contributes to inter-slice discontinuities.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by the original baseline of omitting noise injection in the sampling process and the modified baseline of omitting noise injection along the z-axis.
COST: 75 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that completely eliminating stochasticity along the z-axis will result in better slice consistency metrics than omitting noise injection along this axis, and that the modified baseline of correlated noise injection will fall somewhere in between the two.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating 2D Diffusion Model Accuracy on 3D MPI Data
PROPOSAL: We will apply a state-of-the-art 2D diffusion model to 3D magnetic particle imaging (MPI) data and evaluate its accuracy in reconstructing 3D volumes. MPI data are characterized by high temporal and spatial resolution, making them an ideal candidate for testing 2D diffusion models on volumetric data. We will measure the accuracy of the 2D diffusion model using metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) compared to ground truth and computationally intensive re sampling of slice by slice image interpolation re sampling depth  reconstructions. 
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by previously published diffusion models designed for 3D MPI reconstruction and assess the performance differences.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the 2D diffusion model will be able to provide accurate 3D volume reconstructions for MPI data but may, however, struggle with fine spatial details and maintaining the high resolution in the third dimension. This would suggest a potential limitation of our initial idea to extend a 2D model to the 3D domain via training for merely slice by slice image interpolation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating 3D Physics-Informed Diffusion Models for Medical Imaging
PROPOSAL: We will explore the potential of 3D physics-informed diffusion models for performing 3D medical imaging reconstruction tasks, such as sparse-view and limited-angle CT reconstruction and brain MRI isotropic super-resolution. These models incorporate the underlying physics of the imaging modality into the diffusion process, which can improve the quality of reconstructions. We will compare the performance of our 3D physics-informed diffusion model to state-of-the-art 2D diffusion models and analytical methods for these tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by previous works using analytical and 2D diffusion-based models and assess the performance differences.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the 3D physics-informed diffusion model will outperform the 2D diffusion models in terms of reconstruction quality and accuracy, particularly in applications where physics play a significant role. However, this more sophisticated model may require larger amounts of training data and may not generalize well to unseen tasks.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Investigating 3D Physics-Informed Diffusion Models for Medical Imaging
PROPOSAL: We will refine our previous proposal by incorporating theoretical analysis and investigation of the convergence and stability of the physics-informed diffusion process. This will involve deriving analytical bounds on the propagation of noise and the convergence of the diffusion process in the presence of physical constraints. We will also investigate the impact of different physical constraint formulations on the performance of the 3D physics-informed diffusion model.
CONTROLS: We will draw comparisons to previous works using analytical and 2D diffusion-based models and assess the theoretical validity of our proposed method.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the additional theoretical analysis will reveal challenges in ensuring the stability and convergence of the physics-informed diffusion process, but these challenges can be mitigated through the use of appropriate regularization techniques and adaptive learning rates. By addressing these challenges, we can develop a robust and high-quality 3D physics-informed diffusion model for medical imaging.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Investigating 3D Physics-Informed Diffusion Models for Medical Imaging
PROPOSAL: We will extend our previous proposal by exploring the use of adversarial training to improve the performance and robustness of the 3D physics-informed diffusion model. Adversarial training involves training a discriminator network to distinguish between real and generated data, which can be used to improve the quality of the reconstructions. We will also investigate the use of additional loss functions, such as total variation and perceptual loss, to further improve the performance of the model.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by previous works using analytical and 2D diffusion-based models and assess the performance differences.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the addition of adversarial training and other loss functions will significantly improve the performance and robustness of the 3D physics-informed diffusion model, but may also introduce additional computational complexity and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of 3D Physics-Informed Diffusion Models to Experimental Noise and Image Variability
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the robustness of the 3D physics-informed diffusion model to experimental noise and image variability by injecting different types of noise into the training data and assessing its impact on the reconstruction quality. We will also investigate the model's performance on images with varying levels of skin, skull, and other sources of variability.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by previous works using analytical and 2D diffusion-based models and assess the performance differences.
COST: 275 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the addition of robustness evaluation will reveal challenges in ensuring the model's performance across different scenarios, but by addressing these challenges, we can develop a robust and high-quality 3D physics-informed diffusion model for medical imaging that can handle real-world experimental noise and image variability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Clinical Validation of 3D Diffusion Models for Medical Imaging
PROPOSAL: We will conduct clinical validation of the 3D physics-informed diffusion model on real-world medical imaging datasets, including sparse-view and limited-angle CT reconstruction and brain MRI isotropic super-resolution. We will assess the model's performance on a large set of clinical cases and compare its results to those achieved by standard clinical reconstruction methods. We will also conduct statistical analysis to evaluate the model's accuracy and robustness on a large scale.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those achieved by previous works using analytical and 2D diffusion-based models and assess the performance differences.
COST: 450 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the clinical validation will demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the 3D physics-informed diffusion model on real-world medical imaging datasets, and that the results will have a significant impact on the development of medical imaging technology and clinical practice.
