actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Inter-Slice Inconsistency in 2D Diffusion-Based 3D Medical Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of a standard 2D diffusion-based 3D reconstruction pipeline with that of a modified pipeline where we use a single, global noise schedule across all slices, rather than independent noise schedules for each slice.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline pipeline with independent noise schedules and two additional ablation studies: one where the global noise schedule is trained jointly with the diffusion prior, and one where it is fixed and learned offline.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We hypothesize that using a single global noise schedule will reduce inter-slice inconsistencies and improve the overall quality of the reconstructed volume.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spectral Analysis of Inter-Slice Discontinuities
PROPOSAL: Perform a spectral analysis of the 3D volumes reconstructed using a standard 2D diffusion-based 3D reconstruction pipeline and a pipeline with a single global noise schedule. Specifically, compute the 3D Fourier Transform of the volumes and examine the power spectral densities along the z-axis.
CONTROLS: Compare the spectral characteristics of inter-slice discontinuities against those of true anatomical features.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the inter-slice discontinuities in the standard pipeline are associated with a distinctive spectral signature that is not present in the volumes reconstructed with a global noise schedule.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Spectral Analysis of Inter-Slice Discontinuities
PROPOSAL: Extend the spectral analysis of inter-slice discontinuities to analyze the power spectral densities along the x-y and x-z slices, in addition to the x-y plane. This will provide a more comprehensive understanding of how inter-slice discontinuities manifest in different spatial frequency regimes.
CONTROLS: Compare the spectral characteristics of inter-slice discontinuities against those of true anatomical features.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (increase in computational cost due to increased analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect to find that inter-slice discontinuities exhibit a complex spectral signature that varies across different planes and frequency regimes.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Spectral Analysis of Inter-Slice Discontinuities
PROPOSAL: Extend the spectral analysis of inter-slice discontinuities to analyze the power spectral densities along the x-y and x-z slices, in addition to the x-y plane. This will provide a more comprehensive understanding of how inter-slice discontinuities manifest in different spatial frequency regimes.
CONTROLS: Compare the spectral characteristics of inter-slice discontinuities against those of true anatomical features.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that inter-slice discontinuities exhibit a complex spectral signature that varies across different planes and frequency regimes.

Also,

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Inter-Slice Consistency Using Temporal Synchronization
PROPOSAL: Adapt the temporal synchronization technique used in video restoration to the problem of inter-slice inconsistency in 3D medical reconstruction. Specifically, we will synchronize the stochastic noise components across slices using a learned or predefined schedule.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline pipeline with independent noise schedules and a variant where the global noise schedule is learned jointly with the diffusion prior.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that synchronizing noise components across slices will reduce inter-slice inconsistencies and improve the overall quality of the reconstructed volume.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: 3D Variational Autoencoder for Anatomically-Informed Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Train a 3D variational autoencoder (VAE) on a dataset of ground-truth 3D medical volumes, where the VAE learns to represent the anatomical variability of the training data in a disentangled manner. Then, use the VAE to regularize the 2D diffusion-based 3D reconstruction pipeline, encouraging the model to produce anatomically consistent reconstructions.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline pipeline with no regularization and a variant where the VAE is used in an additional optimization step to post-process the reconstruction.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the VAE regularization module will improve the anatomical consistency of the reconstructed volumes and reduce inter-slice inconsistencies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Explicit Denoising for Improved Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: Instead of using a probabilistic framework (diffusion models) to model the denoising process, we will use a set of explicit denoising filters applied to each slice individually, with the goal of reducing inter-slice inconsistencies. The filters will be learned end-to-end alongside the rest of the 2D diffusion-based 3D reconstruction pipeline.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline pipeline with no denoising filters and a variant where the explicit filters are replaced with a learnable denoising module.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the explicit denoising filters will improve inter-slice consistency and overall quality of the reconstructed volume, although at the potential cost of increased computational complexity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditioning the Diffusion Prior on 3D Spatial Features
PROPOSAL: Introduce a 3D spatial feature encoder that learns to capture structure and consistency in 3D anatomical data. The encoded features will be conditioned on the diffusion prior, allowing it to adapt its noise schedule and denoising process to the local 3D context.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline pipeline with no conditioning module and a variant where the conditioning features are replaced with a limited set of predefined hand-crafted features.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that conditioning the diffusion prior on 3D spatial features will improve inter-slice consistency and overall quality of the reconstructed volume, by enabling the model to capture and propagate 3D anatomical structure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Asynchronous-Parallel Training for Scalable 3D Diffusion-Based Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Train the 3D diffusion-based reconstruction model in an asynchronous-parallel manner, where each slice is processed independently on a separate GPU, reducing the dependency between slices and enabling faster training times for large 3D volumes.
